QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_39

question.text: Using the simple-interest approximation, if the NIFTY spot is at 25,000, risk-free rate 8%, and expected dividend yield 1.5%, what is the theoretical 2-month NIFTY futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: The Series VIII workbook (p.45 and p.56) gives the index/stock futures fair price as F = S × (1 + r - q)^T (or continuous Se^((r-q)T)). The stem explicitly tests the simple-interest approximation F = S × (1 + (r - q) × T): 25,000 × (1 + (0.08 - 0.015) × 2/12) = 25,000 × 1.010833 = 25,270.83. Net carry cost is 6.5% (8% - 1.5%) annualised. The Trap: Rs 25,333.33 ignores dividend yield (uses 8% only). Rs 25,000 assumes no carry. Rs 25,125 uses 1 month instead of 2. The exact compounded value using (1 + r - q)^(2/12) is also very close to 25,270, so the approximation is acceptable here. Note: Source formulae are on Series VIII p.45 (continuous/discrete forms) and p.56 (percentage carry F = S × (1+r)^T).
